name: Arthur Cruttenden
bio: A saddler by trade and a fellow prisoner of Wilde's in Reading, released before him. In June 1897, within weeks of his own release, Wilde had him to stay at Berneval-sur-Mer, tried to find him a friend who could put him back into business, and wrote twice in one day to Reggie Turner to introduce him - once formally, once to say he sang and wrote songs and should be seen "as a friend of mine". Wilde's phrase for him is "gentle and unassuming and grateful", and "very sensitive to kindness". No dates and no later trace survive.
bio_note: From two letters to Reggie Turner of 16 June 1897, both printed on p. 900 and read at the rendered page 2026-08-04; surfaced by the mechanical sweep.
